{{short description|Solution to a partial differential equation which remains close to the initial data}}

In [[mathematical physics]] and the theory of [[partial differential equations]], the [[soliton|solitary wave]] solution of the form <math>u(x,t)=e^{-i\omega t}\phi(x)</math> is said to be '''orbitally stable''' if any solution with the [[initial condition|initial data]] sufficiently close to <math>\phi(x)</math> forever remains in a given small [[Neighbourhood (mathematics)|neighborhood]] of the trajectory of <math>e^{-i\omega t}\phi(x).</math>

==Formal definition==
Formal definition is as follows.<ref>{{cite journal
|author1=Manoussos Grillakis |author2=Jalal Shatah |author3=Walter Strauss  |name-list-style=amp |title=Stability theory of solitary waves in the presence of symmetry
|journal=J. Funct. Anal.
|volume=94
|year=1990
|issue=2 |pages=308–348
|doi=10.1016/0022-1236(90)90016-E |doi-access=free}}</ref> Consider the [[dynamical system]]

:<math>
i\frac{du}{dt}=A(u),
\qquad
u(t)\in X,
\quad t\in\R,
</math>

with <math>X</math> a [[Banach space]] over <math>\Complex</math>, and <math>A : X \to X</math>. We assume that the system is [[unitary invariance|<math>\mathrm{U}(1)</math>-invariant]],
so that
<math>A(e^{is}u) = e^{is}A(u)</math> for any <math>u\in X</math> and any <math>s\in\R</math>.

Assume that <math>\omega \phi=A(\phi)</math>, so that <math>u(t)=e^{-i\omega t}\phi</math> is a solution to the dynamical system.
We call such solution a [[soliton|solitary wave]].

We say that the solitary wave <math>e^{-i\omega t}\phi</math> is orbitally stable if for any <math>\epsilon > 0</math> there is <math>\delta > 0</math> such that for any <math>v_0\in X</math> with <math>\Vert \phi-v_0\Vert_X < \delta</math> there is a solution <math>v(t)</math> defined for all <math>t\ge 0</math> such that <math>v(0) = v_0</math>, and such that this solution satisfies

:<math>\sup_{t\ge 0} \inf_{s\in\R} \Vert v(t) - e^{is} \phi \Vert_X < \epsilon.</math>

==Example==
According to <ref>{{ cite journal
|author1=T. Cazenave  |author2=P.-L. Lions
|name-list-style=amp  |title= Orbital stability of standing waves for some nonlinear Schrödinger equations
|  journal = Comm. Math. Phys.
|  volume = 85
| year = 1982
|number = 4
|pages=549–561
|url=http://projecteuclid.org/getRecord?id=euclid.cmp/1103921547
|bibcode=1982CMaPh..85..549C
|doi = 10.1007/BF01403504 |s2cid=120472894
|url-access=subscription
}}</ref>
,<ref>{{cite journal
|author1=Jerry Bona |author2=Panagiotis Souganidis |author3=Walter Strauss  |name-list-style=amp |title=Stability and instability of solitary waves of Korteweg-de Vries type
|journal=[[Proceedings of the Royal Society A]]
|volume=411
|year=1987
|issue=1841
|pages=395–412
|doi=10.1098/rspa.1987.0073
|bibcode=1987RSPSA.411..395B |s2cid=120894859 }}</ref>
the solitary wave solution <math>e^{-i\omega t}\phi_\omega(x)</math> to the [[nonlinear Schrödinger equation]]
:<math>
i\frac{\partial}{\partial t} u = -\frac{\partial^2}{\partial x^2} u+g\!\left(|u|^2\right)u,
\qquad
u(x,t)\in\Complex,\quad x\in\R,\quad t\in\R,
</math>
where <math>g</math> is a smooth [[real-valued function]], is '''orbitally stable''' if the [[Vakhitov&ndash;Kolokolov stability criterion]] is satisfied:

: <math>\frac{d}{d\omega}Q(\phi_\omega) < 0,</math>

where

: <math>Q(u) = \frac{1}{2} \int_{\R} |u(x,t)|^2 \, dx</math>

is the [[electric charge|charge]] of the solution <math>u(x,t)</math>, which is conserved in time (at least if the solution <math>u(x,t)</math> is sufficiently smooth).

It was also shown,<ref>{{cite journal
    |author = Michael I. Weinstein
     |title = Lyapunov stability of ground states of nonlinear dispersive evolution equations
  |journal = Comm. Pure Appl. Math.
   |volume = 39
     |year = 1986
    |number = 1
     |pages = 51–67
      |doi = 10.1002/cpa.3160390103
}}</ref><ref>{{ Cite book
    |author1=Richard Jordan  |author2=Bruce Turkington
 |name-list-style=amp |chapter = Statistical equilibrium theories for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
 |title = Advances in Wave Interaction and Turbulence
    |location = South Hadley, MA
    |series = Contemp. Math.
    |volume = 283
     |pages= 27–39
      |year = 2001
       |doi = 10.1090/conm/283/04711
|isbn=9780821827147
 }}</ref>
that if <math display="inline">\frac{d}{d\omega}Q(\omega) < 0</math> at a particular value of <math>\omega</math>, then the solitary wave
<math>e^{-i\omega t}\phi_\omega(x)</math> is [[Lyapunov stability|Lyapunov stable]], with the [[Lyapunov function]]
given by <math>L(u) = E(u) - \omega Q(u) + \Gamma(Q(u)-Q(\phi_\omega))^2</math>, where <math>E(u) = \frac{1}{2} \int_{\R} \left(\left|\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}\right|^2 + G\!\left(|u|^2\right)\right) dx</math> is the [[energy]] of a solution <math>u(x,t)</math>, with <math display="inline">G(y) = \int_0^y g(z)\,dz</math> the [[antiderivative]] of <math>g</math>, as long as the constant <math>\Gamma>0</math> is chosen sufficiently large.
